narrative_purpose: Reveals what the exo-pack actually does: it is a filter, not an oxygen tank - drawing in the local air, stripping the poisons, passing the good gas through to the wearer.
subject: A painterly cutaway of an exo-pack mask and its side filter cartridge. Raw, faintly amber-and-green tinged Pandoran air is drawn in at the intake; inside the cartridge it passes through glowing stacked filter beds where dark, heavy toxic motes are caught and held back; clean cool-cyan breathable air flows up through the hose into the clear faceplate, where a calm human face breathes.
scene: A clean, intimate technical cross-section glowing against a dark ground, the flow of air through the stages shown as luminous streams of differing colour.
camera: Side-on cutaway view at mask scale, slightly angled to show the layered filter stages within the cartridge.
light: Internal glow lighting each filter stage; toxic-laden air darker and warmer at the intake, purified air brighter and cooler at the outflow.
palette: Intake air murky amber-green; trapped toxins dark; clean output air bright cyan-teal; dark surround with soft biolum accents.
style: Speculative-biology painterly cutaway plate, hand-painted glowing flows, textured physical hardware.
detail_level: Crisp on the layered filter beds and the colour change of the air through the stages; softer surround.
composition: Air entering from the lower intake, rising from bottom-left through the stacked cartridge stages, into the faceplate at upper right.
consistency_notes: Same exo-pack design as the cover (clear faceplate, side cartridge, jaw hose). The intake-air amber-green and the toxic dark motes match the chapter's carbon-dioxide and hydrogen-sulfide motifs.
